claim: let-7 is one of the most ancient and omnipresent microRNAs.
source: let-7 is one of the most ancient and omnipresent microRNAs, yet relatively little is known about its functional roles in mammalian development and physiology.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about let-7's evolutionary conservation and widespread expression.

claim: let-7 was first identified as a gene that regulates the timing of developmental milestones in a C. elegans screen.
source: let-7 was first identified as a gene that regulates the timing of developmental milestones in a C. elegans screen (Reinhart et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Reinhart et al., 2000.

claim: Mature let-7 is undetectable in early embryos and embryonic stem cells.
source: In mammals, mature let-7 is undetectable in early embryos and embryonic stem cells, but becomes highly expressed in most adult tissues (Schulman et al., 2005; Thomson et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Schulman et al., 2005 and Thomson et al., 2006.

claim: let-7 becomes highly expressed in most adult tissues.
source: In mammals, mature let-7 is undetectable in early embryos and embryonic stem cells, but becomes highly expressed in most adult tissues (Schulman et al., 2005; Thomson et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Schulman et al., 2005 and Thomson et al., 2006.

claim: let-7 has been implicated in body size regulation.
source: A handful of previous studies have implicated let-7 in body size regulation, metabolism, stem cell self-renewal, and colon carcinogenesis (Zhu et al., 2011; Frost and Olson, 2011; Shyh-Chang, et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Madison, et al., 2013, but the core functions of let-7 in regeneration and disease remain incompletely understood.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations including Zhu et al., 2011 and Frost and Olson, 2011.

claim: let-7 has been implicated in metabolism.
source: A handful of previous studies have implicated let-7 in body size regulation, metabolism, stem cell self-renewal, and colon carcinogenesis (Zhu et al., 2011; Frost and Olson, 2011; Shyh-Chang, et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Madison, et al., 2013, but the core functions of let-7 in regeneration and disease remain incompletely understood.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: let-7 has been implicated in stem cell self-renewal.
source: A handful of previous studies have implicated let-7 in body size regulation, metabolism, stem cell self-renewal, and colon carcinogenesis (Zhu et al., 2011; Frost and Olson, 2011; Shyh-Chang, et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Madison, et al., 2013, but the core functions of let-7 in regeneration and disease remain incompletely understood.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations including Shyh-Chang et al., 2013.

claim: let-7 has been implicated in colon carcinogenesis.
source: A handful of previous studies have implicated let-7 in body size regulation, metabolism, stem cell self-renewal, and colon carcinogenesis (Zhu et al., 2011; Frost and Olson, 2011; Shyh-Chang, et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Madison, et al., 2013, but the core functions of let-7 in regeneration and disease remain incompletely understood.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations including Madison et al., 2013.

claim: The let-7 family is comprised of 10 to 12 members in mice and humans.
source: In mice and humans, the let-7 family is comprised of 10 to 12 members who are thought to share a common set of mRNA targets.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the let-7 family composition.

claim: let-7 family members are thought to share a common set of mRNA targets.
source: In mice and humans, the let-7 family is comprised of 10 to 12 members who are thought to share a common set of mRNA targets.
evidence: This is a statement based on established understanding of let-7 family function.

claim: Lin28a inhibits the biogenesis of each let-7 member similarly.
source: Our previous study of Lin28a, which inhibits the biogenesis of each let-7 member similarly (Heo et al., 2008; Nam et al., 2011), suggests that total let-7 dose alterations, rather than regulation of specific members, is important.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Heo et al., 2008 and Nam et al., 2011.

claim: Modest increase in Lin28a and consequent 40% suppression of total let-7 levels promote increased glucose uptake in transgenic mice.
source: In transgenic mice, modest increase in Lin28a and consequent 40% suppression of total let-7 levels promote increased glucose uptake and an overgrowth syndrome (Zhu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhu et al., 2010.

claim: Modest increase in Lin28a and consequent 40% suppression of total let-7 levels promote an overgrowth syndrome in transgenic mice.
source: In transgenic mice, modest increase in Lin28a and consequent 40% suppression of total let-7 levels promote increased glucose uptake and an overgrowth syndrome (Zhu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhu et al., 2010.

claim: let-7s have been implicated as a tumor suppressor predominantly in cell lines and xenograft assays.
source: While let-7s have been implicated as a tumor suppressor, this has predominantly been shown in cell lines and xenograft assays (Guo et al., 2006; Chang et al., 2009; Iliopoulos et al., 2009; Viswanathan et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2010; Lan et al., 2011), as well as using exogenous let-7 delivery to mouse cancer models (Esquela-Kerscher et al., 2008; Trang et al., 2010; Trang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies using cell lines and xenografts.

claim: Exogenous let-7 delivery has been used in mouse cancer models.
source: While let-7s have been implicated as a tumor suppressor, this has predominantly been shown in cell lines and xenograft assays (Guo et al., 2006; Chang et al., 2009; Iliopoulos et al., 2009; Viswanathan et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2010; Lan et al., 2011), as well as using exogenous let-7 delivery to mouse cancer models (Esquela-Kerscher et al., 2008; Trang et al., 2010; Trang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Esquela-Kerscher et al., 2008; Trang et al., 2010; Trang et al., 2011.

claim: Most let-7s are suppressed by more than 60% in the MYC-driven hepatoblastoma model.
source: In this model, most let-7s are suppressed by more than 60% (Nguyen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nguyen et al., 2014.

claim: MYC affects the expression of many other microRNAs.
source: However, MYC affects the expression of many other microRNAs (Chang et al., 2009; Kota et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chang et al., 2009 and Kota et al., 2009.

claim: The precursor microRNA loop of let-7S21L derives from mir-21 and cannot be bound and inhibited by Lin28b.
source: This transgenic form of let-7g is an engineered let-7 species called let-7S21L (let-7g Stem + miR-21 Loop) (Zhu et al., 2011), in which the precursor microRNA loop derives from mir-21 and cannot be bound and inhibited by Lin28b (Figure 1B), which is highly expressed in MYC-driven tumors (Chang et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhu et al., 2011 and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Lin28b is highly expressed in MYC-driven tumors.
source: This transgenic form of let-7g is an engineered let-7 species called let-7S21L (let-7g Stem + miR-21 Loop) (Zhu et al., 2011), in which the precursor microRNA loop derives from mir-21 and cannot be bound and inhibited by Lin28b (Figure 1B), which is highly expressed in MYC-driven tumors (Chang et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chang et al., 2009 and Nguyen et al., 2014.

claim: By 90 days of age, large multifocal tumors had formed in 88% of the MYC alone group.
source: By 90 days of age, large multifocal tumors had formed in 88% of the MYC alone group, whereas single small tumors appeared in only 27% the MYC + let-7S21L group (Figure 1D–F) and overall survival was dramatically improved (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1D-F.

claim: Single small tumors appeared in only 27% of the MYC + let-7S21L group by 90 days of age.
source: By 90 days of age, large multifocal tumors had formed in 88% of the MYC alone group, whereas single small tumors appeared in only 27% the MYC + let-7S21L group (Figure 1D–F) and overall survival was dramatically improved (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1D-F.

claim: Overall survival was dramatically improved in MYC + let-7S21L mice compared to MYC alone mice.
source: By 90 days of age, large multifocal tumors had formed in 88% of the MYC alone group, whereas single small tumors appeared in only 27% the MYC + let-7S21L group (Figure 1D–F) and overall survival was dramatically improved (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The level of let-7g was increased more than eightfold in both non-tumor and tumor tissues in MYC + let-7S21L mice.
source: The level of let-7g was increased more than eightfold in both non-tumor and tumor tissues (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Tumors from both MYC alone and MYC + let-7S21L groups showed similar histology.
source: Tumors from both groups showed similar histology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and MYC expression (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tumors from both MYC alone and MYC + let-7S21L groups showed similar MYC expression.
source: Tumors from both groups showed similar histology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and MYC expression (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Cdc25a is a previously validated let-7 target involved in proliferation and growth.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Johnson et al., 2007.

claim: Cdc34 is a previously validated let-7 target involved in proliferation and growth.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Legesse-Miller et al., 2009.

claim: E2f2 is a previously validated let-7 target involved in proliferation and growth.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dong et al., 2010.

claim: E2f5 is a previously validated let-7 target involved in proliferation and growth.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kropp et al., 2015.

claim: Map4k4 is a previously validated let-7 target involved in proliferation and growth.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tan et al., 2015.

claim: Cdc25a, Cdc34, E2f2, E2f5, and Map4k4 were upregulated in MYC-tumors.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1J-L.

claim: Cdc25a, Cdc34, E2f2, E2f5, and Map4k4 were suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1J-L.

claim: The repression of let-7 targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
source: Gene-expression within tumors showed that previously validated let-7 targets involved in proliferation and growth including Cdc25a (Johnson et al., 2007), Cdc34 (Legesse-Miller et al., 2009), E2f2 (Dong et al., 2010), E2f5 (Kropp et al., 2015), and Map4k4 (Tan et al., 2015) were upregulated in MYC-tumors, but suppressed back down to normal levels in the context of let-7 overexpression (Figure 1J–L), suggesting that the repression of these targets restrains MYC-dependent tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that let-7 overexpression suppresses tumor formation and normalizes target gene expression.

claim: let-7g has potent tumor suppressor activity in the context of MYC-driven hepatoblastoma.
source: These data indicated that let-7g has potent tumor suppressor activity in the context of MYC-driven hepatoblastoma.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced tumor formation and improved survival with let-7g overexpression.

claim: After PHx, let-7s in regenerating tissues fell, but returned to normal after forty hours.
source: After PHx, let-7s in regenerating tissues fell, but returned to normal after forty hours (Figure 2A), findings consistent with a previous report (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and a citation to Chen et al., 2011.

claim: let-7s declined acutely after chemical injury with TCPOBOP.
source: Similarly, let-7s also declined acutely after chemical injury with the xenobiotic TCPOBOP (1,4-bis-[2-[3,5-dichloropyridyloxy]] benzene) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: let-7 increases in a temporally defined fashion during development.
source: This shows that while let-7 increases in a temporally defined fashion during development (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), it can transiently fluctuate after environmental perturbations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: let-7 can transiently fluctuate after environmental perturbations.
source: This shows that while let-7 increases in a temporally defined fashion during development (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), it can transiently fluctuate after environmental perturbations.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing let-7 changes after PHx and TCPOBOP treatment.

claim: Body weight was unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
source: The body weight (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), liver function (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), resected liver mass (Figure 2E) and histology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) were unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Liver function was unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
source: The body weight (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), liver function (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), resected liver mass (Figure 2E) and histology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) were unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Resected liver mass was unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
source: The body weight (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), liver function (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), resected liver mass (Figure 2E) and histology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) were unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Histology was unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
source: The body weight (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), liver function (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), resected liver mass (Figure 2E) and histology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) were unaffected in LAP-let-7S21L mice compared to control mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Forty hours after PHx, there was reduced liver mass in LAP-let-7S21L mice.
source: Forty hours after PHx, there was reduced liver mass and decreased Ki-67 in LAP-let-7S21L mice (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2F-H.

claim: Forty hours after PHx, there was decreased Ki-67 in LAP-let-7S21L mice.
source: Forty hours after PHx, there was reduced liver mass and decreased Ki-67 in LAP-let-7S21L mice (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2F-H.

claim: Liver mass was no different at four and fourteen days after PHx in LAP-let-7S21L mice, indicating a kinetic delay but not a permanent impairment.
source: Liver mass was no different at four and fourteen days, indicating a kinetic delay but not a permanent impairment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F,G and inference about the nature of the effect.

claim: let-7g microRNA mimics inhibited liver regeneration after PHx.
source: let-7g, but not control mimics, inhibited regeneration (Figure 2I–K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2I-K.

claim: let-7 overexpression blocked MYC-induced tumorigenesis.
source: While let-7 overexpression blocked MYC-induced tumorigenesis, these data show that a similar increase in let-7 levels inhibited post-injury organ growth and regeneration.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the MYC tumor model.

claim: A similar increase in let-7 levels inhibited post-injury organ growth and regeneration.
source: While let-7 overexpression blocked MYC-induced tumorigenesis, these data show that a similar increase in let-7 levels inhibited post-injury organ growth and regeneration.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the PHx experiments.

claim: let-7 is one of the most highly expressed microRNA families in the liver.
source: Small RNA-sequencing data from Xie et al. showed that let-7 is one of the most highly expressed microRNA families in the liver and that let-7b and let-7c2 together comprise approximately 18% of the let-7 total (Figure 3B) (Xie et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xie et al., 2012 and data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: let-7b and let-7c2 together comprise approximately 18% of the let-7 total in the liver.
source: Small RNA-sequencing data from Xie et al. showed that let-7 is one of the most highly expressed microRNA families in the liver and that let-7b and let-7c2 together comprise approximately 18% of the let-7 total (Figure 3B) (Xie et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xie et al., 2012 and data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: let-7b/c2 LKO mice have substantial, but far from a complete reduction of total let-7 levels.
source: Thus, let-7b/c2 LKO mice have substantial, but far from a complete reduction of total let-7 levels.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the fact that let-7b and let-7c2 comprise only 18% of total let-7.

claim: let-7b/c2 LKO mice were healthy and showed normal liver/body weight ratios at baseline.
source: These LKO mice were healthy and showed normal liver/body weight ratios and histology at baseline (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: let-7b/c2 LKO mice showed normal histology at baseline.
source: These LKO mice were healthy and showed normal liver/body weight ratios and histology at baseline (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: An identical amount of liver mass was resected from let-7b/c2Fl/Fl control and let-7b/c2 LKO mice.
source: An identical amount of liver mass was resected from let-7b/c2Fl/Fl control and let-7b/c2 LKO mice (Figure 3C,D), but LKO mice exhibited significant increases in liver mass and proliferation 40 hr after surgery (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3C,D.

claim: let-7b/c2 LKO mice exhibited significant increases in liver mass 40 hr after surgery.
source: An identical amount of liver mass was resected from let-7b/c2Fl/Fl control and let-7b/c2 LKO mice (Figure 3C,D), but LKO mice exhibited significant increases in liver mass and proliferation 40 hr after surgery (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3E-G.

claim: let-7b/c2 LKO mice exhibited significant increases in proliferation 40 hr after surgery.
source: An identical amount of liver mass was resected from let-7b/c2Fl/Fl control and let-7b/c2 LKO mice (Figure 3C,D), but LKO mice exhibited significant increases in liver mass and proliferation 40 hr after surgery (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3E-G.

claim: Four and seven days after PHx, there were no differences in liver weights between control and let-7b/c2 LKO mice, indicating that other phases of regeneration were unaffected.
source: Four and seven days after PHx, there were no differences in liver weights, indicating that other phases of regeneration were unaffected (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D and inference about regeneration phases.

claim: At fourteen days after PHx, the liver weight precisely achieved pre-surgery levels in control and LKO mice, indicating accelerated but not excessive regeneration.
source: At fourteen days, the liver weight precisely achieved pre-surgery levels in control and LKO mice, indicating accelerated but not excessive regeneration (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D and inference about the nature of regeneration.

claim: There was no compensatory upregulation of other let-7s in pre- or post-PHx tissues in let-7b/c2 LKO mice.
source: There was no compensatory upregulation of other let-7s in pre- or post-PHx tissues (Figure 3H), supporting the concept that let-7 is a dose-dependent regeneration suppressor.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: let-7 is a dose-dependent regeneration suppressor.
source: There was no compensatory upregulation of other let-7s in pre- or post-PHx tissues (Figure 3H), supporting the concept that let-7 is a dose-dependent regeneration suppressor.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that partial reduction of let-7 enhances regeneration without compensatory changes.

claim: Cre under the Albumin promoter is expressed in embryonic hepatoblasts that give rise to both hepatocyte and bile duct compartments.
source: Cre under the Albumin promoter is expressed in embryonic hepatoblasts that give rise to both hepatocyte and bile duct compartments (Postic and Magnuson, 1999, 2000; Xu et al., 2006; Weisend et al., 2009; Malato et al., 2011), so developmental influences of let-7 loss could have led to adult phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies characterizing Albumin-Cre expression.

claim: AAV8.TBG.PI.Cre.rBG mediates efficient gene excision in hepatocytes but never in biliary epithelial cells.
source: To define cell- and temporal-specific roles of let-7b/c2, we used adeno-associated virus expressing Cre (AAV8.TBG.PI.Cre.rBG, hereafter called "AAV-Cre"), known to mediate efficient gene excision in hepatocytes but never in biliary epithelial cells (Yanger et al., 2013) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yanger et al., 2013 and data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Adult and hepatocyte-specific conditional knockout mice exhibited significantly enhanced regenerative capacity.
source: These adult and hepatocyte-specific conditional knockout mice also exhibited significantly enhanced regenerative capacity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C-F.

claim: Knockdown of let-7a in SV40 immortalized hepatocytes led to increased proliferation.
source: To test if proliferative effects are specific to particular let-7 species, we knocked-down either let-7a or let-7b in SV40 immortalized hepatocytes (H2.35 cells) and found that both led to increased proliferation (Figure 3I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Knockdown of let-7b in SV40 immortalized hepatocytes led to increased proliferation.
source: To test if proliferative effects are specific to particular let-7 species, we knocked-down either let-7a or let-7b in SV40 immortalized hepatocytes (H2.35 cells) and found that both led to increased proliferation (Figure 3I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Physiological let-7 levels regulate the kinetics of adult liver regeneration by hepatocytes.
source: Collectively, our data shows that physiological let-7 levels regulate the kinetics of adult liver regeneration by hepatocytes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the collective experimental data showing effects of let-7 manipulation on regeneration.

claim: let-7 was previously demonstrated to regulate the insulin-PI3K-mTOR pathway.
source: let-7 was previously demonstrated to regulate the insulin-PI3K-mTOR pathway (Zhu et al., 2011; Frost and Olson, 2011), which is also important in liver regeneration (Okano et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2009; Haga et al., 2009; Espeillac et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhu et al., 2011 and Frost and Olson, 2011.

claim: The insulin-PI3K-mTOR pathway is important in liver regeneration.
source: let-7 was previously demonstrated to regulate the insulin-PI3K-mTOR pathway (Zhu et al., 2011; Frost and Olson, 2011), which is also important in liver regeneration (Okano et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2009; Haga et al., 2009; Espeillac et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Okano et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2009; Haga et al., 2009; Espeillac et al., 2011.

claim: In regenerating livers treated with let-7g mimic, there was significant protein suppression of insulin receptor β, Igf1rβ, and Irs2.
source: In regenerating livers treated with let-7g mimic (Figure 2I–K), we found significant protein suppression of insulin receptor β, Igf1rβ, and Irs2, previously validated let-7 targets at the top of the insulin pathway (Figure 4A,B) (Zhu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4A,B.

claim: Insulin receptor β, Igf1rβ, and Irs2 are previously validated let-7 targets at the top of the insulin pathway.
source: In regenerating livers treated with let-7g mimic (Figure 2I–K), we found significant protein suppression of insulin receptor β, Igf1rβ, and Irs2, previously validated let-7 targets at the top of the insulin pathway (Figure 4A,B) (Zhu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhu et al., 2011.

claim: The expression of cell cycle genes (Ccnb1, Cdc34, and Cdk8) and Map4k4 were downregulated in let-7g overexpressing livers.
source: In addition to insulin signaling components, the expression of cell cycle genes (Ccnb1, Cdc34, and Cdk8) and Map4k4 were also downregulated (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In mice with acute let-7b/c2 deletion by AAV-Cre, there was a small increase in insulin receptor β protein levels.
source: In mice with acute let-7b/c2 deletion by AAV-Cre (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), there was a small increase in insulin receptor β protein levels (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4D,E.

claim: Increased mTOR signaling was evident in the increased phospho-S6K/Total S6K and phospho-S6/Total S6 ratios in let-7b/c2 knockout livers.
source: Increased mTOR signaling was also evident in the increased phospho-S6K/Total S6K and phospho-S6/Total S6 ratios (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E (note: this appears to be a typo in the manuscript, should be Figure 4E based on context).

claim: Rapamycin abrogated differences in regenerating liver weights between control and LKO mice.
source: Rapamycin abrogated differences in regenerating liver weights between control and LKO mice (Figure 4F), demonstrating that let-7b/c2 loss promotes additional mTOR activation to enhance regeneration.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: let-7b/c2 loss promotes additional mTOR activation to enhance regeneration.
source: Rapamycin abrogated differences in regenerating liver weights between control and LKO mice (Figure 4F), demonstrating that let-7b/c2 loss promotes additional mTOR activation to enhance regeneration.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that mTOR inhibition eliminates the regenerative advantage of let-7 loss.

claim: Rapamycin's allosteric inhibition of mTOR can lead to pleiotropic and unpredictable effects due to cell-type specific and feedback related phenomena.

claim: mTOR is hyperactivated in LKO livers.

claim: Histology showed prominent microvesicular steatosis in Rosa-let-7S21L mice after let-7g induction.

claim: Microvesicular steatosis is characterized by intra-cytoplasmic lipid droplets.

claim: Liver dysfunction was not seen after low-dose let-7 overexpression in LAP-let-7S21L mice.

claim: Mice receiving let-7g mimic lost significantly more weight than control mice.

source: Mice receiving let-7g mimic lost significantly more weight (Figure 5F) and suffered hepatocyte destruction leading to increased AST/ALT levels (Figure 5G), while control mice remained healthy.

claim: Mimic delivery achieved a twelvefold increase of let-7g.

claim: Only 1 of 12 (7.7%) of the non-induced mice had any tumors over 18 months.

claim: Chronic let-7 overexpression likely caused hepatocyte toxicity and selected for pre-malignant hepatocytes that eventually become cancer.
source: Chronic let-7 overexpression likely caused hepatocyte toxicity and selected for pre-malignant hepatocytes that eventually become cancer.

claim: Deep redundancy of multiple highly conserved genes raises the possibility that dose regulation is important.
source: Deep redundancy of multiple highly conserved genes raises the possibility that dose regulation is important.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the biological significance of gene redundancy.

claim: Overexpression has been helpful in uncovering physiological functions of let-7.
source: Despite this, overexpression has been helpful in uncovering physiological functions of let-7 (Zhu et al., 2011; Frost and Olson, 2011; Shyh-Chang et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2013; Madison et al., 2013).

claim: let-7 suppression is a fundamental requirement for MYC-mediated liver transformation.
source: Using overexpression tools, we have shown that let-7 suppression is a fundamental requirement for MYC-mediated liver transformation, and that let-7 is capable of counteracting strong oncogenic drivers in vivo.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that let-7 overexpression blocks MYC-driven tumorigenesis.

claim: let-7 is capable of counteracting strong oncogenic drivers in vivo.
source: Using overexpression tools, we have shown that let-7 suppression is a fundamental requirement for MYC-mediated liver transformation, and that let-7 is capable of counteracting strong oncogenic drivers in vivo.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that let-7 overexpression blocks MYC-driven tumorigenesis.

claim: The loss of two out of the ten let-7 members in the liver resulted in improved liver proliferation and regeneration.
source: More surprisingly, our knockout mouse model showed that the loss of two out of the ten let-7 members in the liver resulted in improved liver proliferation and regeneration.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the let-7b/c2 LKO mice.

claim: There is a lack of complete redundancy between let-7 microRNA species.
source: These data suggest a lack of complete redundancy between let-7 microRNA species, but rather a precisely regulated cumulative dose that when increased or decreased, leads to significant alterations in regenerative capacity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that partial reduction of let-7 has functional consequences.

claim: let-7 is regulated as a precisely regulated cumulative dose that when increased or decreased, leads to significant alterations in regenerative capacity.
source: These data suggest a lack of complete redundancy between let-7 microRNA species, but rather a precisely regulated cumulative dose that when increased or decreased, leads to significant alterations in regenerative capacity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing dose-dependent effects of let-7 on regeneration.

claim: In tissues where malignancies arise from chronically injured tissues, winners of the competition between cancer and host cells might ultimately dictate whether organ failure or tumor progression ensues.
source: In these tissues, winners of the competition between cancer and host cells might ultimately dictate whether organ failure or tumor progression ensues.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the dynamics of cancer development in injured tissues.

claim: It has been thought that one key advantage of using microRNAs therapeutically is that they are already expressed at high levels in normal tissues, thus making increased dosing likely to be safe and tolerable.
source: It has been thought that one key advantage of using microRNAs therapeutically is that they are already expressed at high levels in normal tissues, thus making increased dosing likely to be safe and tolerable.
evidence: This is a statement of a prevailing assumption in the field about microRNA therapeutics.

claim: Chronic let-7 overexpression caused hepatotoxicity, disrupted tissue homeostasis, ultimately leading to carcinogenesis.
source: Surprisingly, we showed that chronic let-7 overexpression caused hepatotoxicity, disrupted tissue homeostasis, ultimately leading to carcinogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the Rosa-let-7S21L mice.

source: This is likely due to the high levels of overexpression achieved in the Rosa-rtTA transgenic system, as opposed to the lower dose in the LAP-tTA system.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of toxicity outcomes between the two systems with different expression levels.

claim: High doses of let-7 are likely to be toxic to hepatocytes.
source: These high doses are likely to be toxic to hepatocytes, a phenomena compounded by the fact that excess let-7 impairs proliferation in surviving cells that might serve to replenish lost tissues.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing hepatotoxicity at high let-7 doses.

claim: Excess let-7 impairs proliferation in surviving cells that might serve to replenish lost tissues.
source: These high doses are likely to be toxic to hepatocytes, a phenomena compounded by the fact that excess let-7 impairs proliferation in surviving cells that might serve to replenish lost tissues.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing impaired regeneration with let-7 overexpression.

source: Rosa-rtTA does induce expression in cells other than hepatocytes and bile duct epithelia, leaving the possibility that non-cell autonomous influences of let-7 overexpression play a role in liver injury and cancer development.

source: A more interesting possibility would be if distinct genetic subtypes of cancer respond differently to let-7 overexpression.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about potential context-dependent effects of let-7.

claim: let-7 has been conceptualized as a general tumor suppressor.
source: Since let-7 has been conceptualized as a general tumor suppressor, it is surprising that it can cause opposing phenotypes in distinct cancer models.
evidence: This is a statement of a prevailing view in the field about let-7's role.

claim: MYC liver cancers show a dramatic suppression of let-7, rendering it especially sensitive to let-7 replacement.
source: MYC liver cancers show a dramatic suppression of let-7, rendering it especially sensitive to let-7 replacement.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing let-7 suppression in MYC tumors and their sensitivity to let-7 overexpression.

claim: Tumors or tissues with more normal levels of let-7 might not respond to increases in let-7.
source: Tumors or tissues with more normal levels of let-7 might not respond to increases in let-7.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about potential context-dependent effects of let-7.

source: Alternatively, the growth of other cancer models may not depend on the overproduction of let-7 target genes/proteins.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about potential mechanisms underlying differential cancer responses to let-7.

source: let-7 overexpression in these contexts would probably not elicit growth suppression, but may instead exacerbate tissue injury.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental observations of let-7-induced hepatotoxicity.

source: Together, our data suggest that let-7 therapy directed at hepatocellular carcinomas could be risky, given that most of these cancers occur in severely compromised, cirrhotic livers (Yang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing hepatotoxicity with let-7 overexpression and knowledge about HCC context, supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2011.

claim: Most hepatocellular carcinomas occur in severely compromised, cirrhotic livers.
source: Together, our data suggest that let-7 therapy directed at hepatocellular carcinomas could be risky, given that most of these cancers occur in severely compromised, cirrhotic livers (Yang et al., 2011).

claim: The total dose of let-7 is evolutionarily determined via regulation of the expression levels of individual let-7 members.
source: We speculate that the total dose of let-7 is evolutionarily determined via regulation of the expression levels of individual let-7 members, and is postnatally maintained at a level that can suppress cancer, but which also allows for adequate levels of mammalian regenerative capacity.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental observations of dose-dependent let-7 effects.

claim: let-7 is postnatally maintained at a level that can suppress cancer, but which also allows for adequate levels of mammalian regenerative capacity.
source: We speculate that the total dose of let-7 is evolutionarily determined via regulation of the expression levels of individual let-7 members, and is postnatally maintained at a level that can suppress cancer, but which also allows for adequate levels of mammalian regenerative capacity.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental observations showing a balance between tumor suppression and regeneration.

claim: let-7 levels are dynamic after environmental perturbations.
source: Clearly, let-7 levels are not static throughout life, since let-7 levels are dynamic after environmental perturbations.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing let-7 changes after PHx and TCPOBOP treatment.

claim: When baseline let-7 levels are altered permanently by genetic means, compromises in tumor suppression or tissue regeneration were revealed.
source: However, when baseline let-7 levels are altered permanently by genetic means, compromises in tumor suppression or tissue regeneration were revealed.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the genetic models showing effects on both tumorigenesis and regeneration.

claim: Modest let-7 overexpression abrogated MYC-driven liver cancer by antagonizing multiple let-7 sensitive oncogenes.
source: Modest let-7 overexpression abrogated MYC-driven liver cancer by antagonizing multiple let-7 sensitive oncogenes.

claim: The same level of let-7 overexpression that abrogated MYC-driven liver cancer blocked liver regeneration.
source: However, the same level of overexpression blocked liver regeneration, while let-7 deletion enhanced it, demonstrating that distinct let-7 levels can mediate desirable phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the PHx experiments.

claim: let-7 deletion enhanced liver regeneration.
source: However, the same level of overexpression blocked liver regeneration, while let-7 deletion enhanced it, demonstrating that distinct let-7 levels can mediate desirable phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the let-7b/c2 LKO mice.

claim: Distinct let-7 levels can mediate desirable phenotypes.
source: However, the same level of overexpression blocked liver regeneration, while let-7 deletion enhanced it, demonstrating that distinct let-7 levels can mediate desirable phenotypes.

claim: let-7 dependent regeneration phenotypes resulted from influences on the insulin-PI3K-mTOR pathway.
source: let-7 dependent regeneration phenotypes resulted from influences on the insulin-PI3K-mTOR pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing effects on insulin pathway components and mTOR signaling, and the functional effects of mTOR inhibitors.

claim: Chronic high-dose let-7 overexpression caused liver damage and degeneration, paradoxically leading to tumorigenesis.
source: We found that chronic high-dose let-7 overexpression caused liver damage and degeneration, paradoxically leading to tumorigenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the Rosa-let-7S21L mice showing hepatotoxicity and tumor development.

claim: Too little or too much let-7 resulted in compromised protection against cancer or tissue damage, respectively.
source: Too little or too much let-7 resulted in compromised protection against cancer or tissue damage, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing increased cancer risk with let-7 loss and tissue damage with high-dose let-7 overexpression.

claim: let-7 performs tumor suppressive roles at the expense of regeneration.
source: Here, analysis of mouse models revealed that let-7, a large and ancient microRNA family, performs tumor suppressive roles at the expense of regeneration.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that let-7 levels that suppress tumors also impair regeneration.

claim: These dose-dependent roles for let-7 in tissue repair and tumorigenesis rationalize the tight regulation of this microRNA in development.
source: These dose-dependent roles for let-7 in tissue repair and tumorigenesis rationalize the tight regulation of this microRNA in development, and have important implications for let-7 based therapeutics.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing dose-dependent effects and their implications.

claim: The dose-dependent roles for let-7 have important implications for let-7 based therapeutics.
source: These dose-dependent roles for let-7 in tissue repair and tumorigenesis rationalize the tight regulation of this microRNA in development, and have important implications for let-7 based therapeutics.
